title: The Four Winds
notes: This chunk delivers a dense, assertive identification of the four winds as throne-commissioned spirits, chaining Zechariah’s chariots, the horsemen, Ezekiel’s judgments, scatter/gather texts, east-wind judgments, and the sealing restraint with clean symbol links and law-positive force. Scripture blocks and internal cross-references are accurate and well-placed. Residual defects are three author-prose And-openers (two of them presenter-style “mark” cues that stage the reader), one missing relative pronoun that leaves an appositive dangling, and a modern marriage idiom that jars the register. Surgical replacements restore house style and clarity without altering doctrine, quotes, or density.

proposals.old: And all wind answers to its Maker — He rebukes even a literal storm, __“Peace, be still,”__ and it obeys (Mark 4:39); the more so these spirit-winds He sends and recalls.
proposals.new: All wind answers to its Maker — He rebukes even a literal storm, __“Peace, be still,”__ and it obeys (Mark 4:39); the more so these spirit-winds He sends and recalls.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences starting with And; the claim stands stronger and cleaner without the conjunction.

proposals.old: from the four _corners_ of the earth where the dispersed wait (Isaiah 11:12), corners the link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[Wings] chapter searched; the winds sweep the quarters, and the quarters give up their gleanings.
proposals.new: from the four _corners_ of the earth where the dispersed wait (Isaiah 11:12), corners that the link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[Wings] chapter searched; the winds sweep the quarters, and the quarters give up their gleanings.
proposals.rationale: The appositive lacks “that,” leaving the clause ungrammatical and the reference to the Wings chapter dangling.

proposals.old: And mark who waits at the corners: on the garment, the corner is where the law hangs its reminder — __“that ye may look upon it, and *remember all the commandments* of the LORD”__ (Numbers 15:39) — and at the earth's four wings wait __“the remnant… which *keep the commandments* of God”__ (Revelation 12:17).
proposals.new: At the corners wait those who keep the commandments: on the garment, the corner is where the law hangs its reminder — __“that ye may look upon it, and *remember all the commandments* of the LORD”__ (Numbers 15:39) — and at the earth's four wings wait __“the remnant… which *keep the commandments* of God”__ (Revelation 12:17).
proposals.summary: Remove director cue and And-start; assert the remnant identification.
proposals.rationale: House style bans “mark” staging and And-openers; the rewrite keeps the garment/earth parallel and density while stating the claim directly.

proposals.old: And mark where the scene stands: after the sixth seal is opened (Revelation 6:12) — the riders commissioned at the first four seals are still reined in at the four corners when the sixth is broken.
proposals.new: The scene stands after the sixth seal is opened (Revelation 6:12) — the riders commissioned at the first four seals are still reined in at the four corners when the sixth is broken.
proposals.rationale: Staging language and prohibited opener violate house style; the factual placement of the scene remains intact and assertive.

proposals.old: Jesus had already tied the knot for Nicodemus: __“The *wind* bloweth where it listeth… so is every one that is *born of the Spirit*”__ (John 3:8) — one word for wind and Spirit, in Hebrew and in Greek alike.
proposals.new: Jesus had already joined wind and Spirit for Nicodemus: __“The *wind* bloweth where it listeth… so is every one that is *born of the Spirit*”__ (John 3:8) — one word for wind and Spirit, in Hebrew and in Greek alike.
proposals.summary: Replace marriage idiom with direct join.
proposals.rationale: The modern “tied the knot” cliché jars against the biblical register and confuses the intended identification of wind with Spirit.
